t:
As shown in the figure, a chain of mass m is placed on a smooth quarter circular portion of radius R. End A is tied with a wedge while the remaining chain is free, then the minimum work required to be done by the external agent to make the chain horizontal keeping point A fixed, is
[[img:51e72b3a23f3]]
s:
Let the horizontal level passing through point A be the reference for zero gravitational potential energy.
The center of mass of a uniform quarter circular chain of radius R is located at a distance of 2R/π from its center of curvature.
From the given geometry, the center of curvature lies on the horizontal line extending from A to the right. Thus, the center of mass of the initial chain configuration is at a vertical depth of 2R/π below point A.
The initial potential energy of the chain is Uᵢ=−mg(2R/π).
When the chain is pulled to become horizontal while keeping point A fixed, it will lie completely on the reference level. The final potential energy of the chain is U_f=0.
The minimum work required by the external agent is equal to the change in potential energy of the system.
W=ΔU=U_f−Uᵢ
W=0−(−mg2R/π)=mg2R/π

t:
A 1 kg particle at a height of 8 m has a speed of 10 m/s down a fixed incline making an angle 53° with horizontal as shown in figure. It slides on a horizontal section of length 10 m at ground level and then up a fixed incline making an angle 37° with horizontal. All surfaces have μₖ=0.5. How far (in meters) from point O (bottom of right inclined plane), along the incline making an angle 37° with horizontal, does the particle first come to rest?
[[img:d5254b6b6d26]]
s:
Initial mechanical energy: Uᵢ=mgh=1×10×8=80 J, Kᵢ=1/2mv²=1/2(1)(10)²=50 J
Eᵢ=80+50=130 J
Friction on first incline (53°): d₁=8/(sin53°)=8/(4/5)=10 m
N₁=mgcos53°=(1)(10)(3/5)=6 N
W_(f1)=−μₖN₁d₁=−(0.5)(6)(10)=−30 J
Friction on horizontal section: d₂=10 m
N₂=mg=10 N
W_(f2)=−(0.5)(10)(10)=−50 J
Energy at point O: E_O=130−30−50=50 J
On second incline (37°), particle travels distance s until it stops:
U_f=mgssin37°=(1)(10)(s)(3/5)=6s J
N₃=mgcos37°=(1)(10)(4/5)=8 N
W_(f3)=−(0.5)(8)(s)=−4s J
Applying Work-Energy theorem: U_f−E_O=W_(f3)
6s−50=−4s⇒10s=50⇒s=5 m
Correct option: (4)

t: A steel ball of mass 5 g is thrown downward with velocity 10 m/s from height 19.5 m. It penetrates sand by 50 cm. The change in mechanical energy (in joule) will be (g=10 m/s²)

A block of mass 3 kg is placed at the origin at t=0 with an initial velocity of 6√3 m/s in the positive x-direction. The only force acting on it is conservative, and its potential energy is defined as U=−x³+9x²+20 (SI units). What is its velocity when its retardation is maximum after t=0?
s:
Given the potential energy U(x)=−x³+9x²+20, the conservative force acting on the block is:
F=−dU/dx=3x²−18x
Since the mass of the block is m=3 kg, the acceleration a is:
a=F/m=(3x²−18x)/3=x²−6x
The retardation r=−a is:
r=6x−x²
For the retardation to be maximum, dr/dx=0:
6−2x=0⇒x=3 m
At x=0, the potential energy is:
U(0)=20 J
At x=3 m, the potential energy is:
U(3)=−(3)³+9(3)²+20=−27+81+20=74 J
By conservation of mechanical energy between x=0 and x=3 m:
Kᵢ+U(0)=K_f+U(3)
1/2mu²+20=1/2mv²+74
Substituting m=3 kg and u=6√3 m/s:
1/2(3)(6√3)²+20=1/2(3)v²+74
3/2(108)+20=3/2v²+74
162+20=3/2v²+74
3/2v²=182−74=108
v²=72⇒v=√72 m/s

t: A ball of mass m moving with a constant velocity strikes against a ball of same mass at rest. If e = coefficient of restitution, then what will be the ratio of velocity v₁/v₂ of two balls after collision?
s:
As u₂=0 and m₁=m₂, therefore from m₁u₁+m₂u₂=m₁v₁+m₂v₂
we get u₁=v₁+v₂
Also, e=(v₂−v₁)/u₁=(v₂−v₁)/(v₂+v₁)=(1−v₁/v₂)/(1+v₁/v₂),
which gives v₁/v₂=(1−e)/(1+e)

t: A bullet is fired from a rifle which recoils after firing. The ratio of the kinetic energy of the rifle to that of the bullet is
s:
Let M be the mass of the rifle and m that of the bullet and let V and v be their respective speeds. From the principle of conservation of momentum, we have MV=mv. The ratio of their kinetic energies is
Kᵣ/K_b=(1/2MV²)/(1/2mv²)=MV²/mv²=((MV)²)/((mv)²)⋅m/M=m/M
Since m<M,Kᵣ<K_b. Hence the correct choice is (c).

t: The pilot of an aircraft, who is not tied to his seat, can loop a vertical circle in air without falling out at the top of the loop. What is the minimum speed required so that he can successfully negotiate a loop of radius 4 km? Take g=10 ms⁻²
s:
The pilot does not drop down when he is at the top of the loop because his weight mg is less than the centripetal force mv²/R required to keep him in the loop. The rest of the centripetal force is balanced by the reaction of the seat. Hence, he is stuck to the seat without being tied to it. If the speed of the aircraft is reduced so that mg>mv²/R, he will fall off from his seat. Therefore, the minimum speed vₘᵢₙ required to successfully negotiate the vertical loop is given by
mg=mvₘᵢₙ²/R

Thus, the correct choice is (b). .
